clue.text: No. 78, fruit in a can? On the contrary, outranking …

indicators.note: the clue says the fruit goes in the can, signalling one piece placed inside another
reverses the stated relationship, so the can goes inside the fruit instead

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
taken as written
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A setter teases about tinned fruit while starting a chain of medal rankings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' alone would put the fruit inside the can, but 'On the contrary' flips it. 'outranking …' runs on into the next clue, since this metal ranks above gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is the chemical element with atomic number 78.

clue.text: … No. 79, first, and …

definitions.meaning: the medal awarded for first place

explanation.definitionFit: Gold is element 79, and a gold medal is the award for coming first.

clue.text: … No. 47, second

definitions.meaning: the medal awarded for second place

explanation.definitionFit: Silver is element 47, and a silver medal is the award for coming second.

clue.text: Riposte with sword, retaining skill with right opening

indicators.note: right comes at the opening, the start of the answer
the sword holds onto the skill, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword
art means skill

explanation.surface: A fencer's witty reply, delivered sword in hand with deft footwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick witty reply, so a riposte in conversation is a synonym.

clue.text: Doctors No. 11, mostly additive to food

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor; read as 'Doctor's'
the abbreviation read as the word no
sodium is the element with atomic number 11

explanation.surface: Medics prescribe element 11 as a food additive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' belongs to the definition: this word is most of the name of the additive monosodium glutamate (MSG).
explanation.definitionFit: Monosodium glutamate is a flavour enhancer, and this word makes up most of its name.

clue.text: No. 53 has 10 to eat

parts.note: the digits 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Element 53 is said to take a meal with the number ten.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria's trick: '10' written in digits looks like the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine is the chemical element with atomic number 53.

clue.text: No. 9's illness or mine, first off

parts.note: flu is an illness
taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of the word mine is taken off

explanation.surface: Someone compares element 9 to a disease or a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluorine is the chemical element with atomic number 9; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Making 'ole in place of films?

indicators.note: whole with its H dropped, Cockney style, tells us to drop the H from the word too

parts.note: making whole means healing

explanation.surface: A Cockney talks of mending a hole at the film studios.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making 'ole' is 'making whole', HEALING, said with a dropped H. Ealing Studios in west London made the famous Ealing comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Ealing, in west London, is home to Ealing Studios, a historic centre of British film-making.

clue.text: Treat disease with drug backed by crab's foot?

indicators.note: the whole sequence is turned back to front

parts.note: to do can mean to treat or deal with
pox is a disease
E is ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: Advice to cure an illness by medicating, apparently via a crab's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns the whole run round, giving EXOPOD from the three pieces. The question mark warns that an exopod is a branch of a crustacean's limb, not strictly a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: An exopod is the outer branch of a crustacean limb, so a crab's leg part.

clue.text: Fixer for breeders?

parts.note: reads as a fixer who works for breeders, but combines a collar fastener with an establishment where animals are kept for breeding

explanation.definitionFit: A stud is both a small fastener and a place where horses are bred.

clue.text: Boy's love left in sound Spanish city

indicators.note: the three pieces go inside the word meaning sound

parts.note: valid means sound, as a sound argument
a lad is a boy
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A boy's love affair has been left inside a sound Spanish setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Valladolid is a city in north-western Spain.

clue.text: Device for ship in Sri Lanka port, reportedly

clue.text: How difficult without aspiration to rule (the Tories?) in the old TV serial

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: aspiration is the sound of H, so the letter H is dropped

parts.note: hard means difficult
to sway is to rule or hold power

explanation.surface: A political jibe asks how hard it is for the Tories to rule.
explanation.walkthrough: '(the Tories?)' hints at Michael Howard, then Conservative leader, whose 'way' of ruling the party is the pun. Howards' Way was a BBC drama of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Howards' Way was a BBC television drama series about boatbuilders, running 1985 to 1990.

clue.text: No. 7, otherwise 9, taking in opening for cave-dweller

indicators.note: the rearranged number takes the other piece inside it
signals the letters of the number word arranged in another way

parts.note: the number nine spelt out

indicators.note: only the opening part of the cave-dweller word is kept

parts.note: a troglodyte lives in a cave

explanation.surface: Element 7 is linked to the number nine and to a caveman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges the number into NIEN; 'opening for' keeps only the start of the cave-dweller word (itself slang for one), which 'taking in' puts in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is the chemical element with atomic number 7.

clue.text: Fretful baby left fretful cat outside

indicators.note: the cat goes outside, around the letter for left

parts.note: a mewer is one that mews, a complaining cat

explanation.surface: A crying infant has been abandoned with an anxious cat around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mewler is one who whimpers or cries feebly, as a fretful baby does.

clue.text: Basis of meringues, for example, each way without a particle

parts.note: EG again, this time read backwards

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other
the abbreviation is read in both directions, forwards and then backwards

parts.note: EG again, this time read backwards
a whit is a tiny particle, the least bit

explanation.surface: A recipe note about meringues, with a betting term and a particle thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each way' looks like the betting phrase, but asks for EG forwards and backwards: EG then GE, and GE goes 'without' (outside) WHIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Meringue is made by whisking egg white with sugar, so it is the basis.

clue.text: No. 2's first turn in device for ship

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the steering device

parts.note: the helm steers a ship
I is the Roman numeral one, first
U as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: Element 2 takes its first turn at the ship's controls.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium is the chemical element with atomic number 2; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: The Guardian's name in China is black

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for China

parts.note: Ming is the Chinese dynasty, and Ming china is porcelain
from the paper's own point of view, ours

explanation.surface: The newspaper's name is apparently blacked in China.
explanation.definitionFit: Mourning dress is traditionally black, so being in mourning means being in black.

clue.text: Girl in England? Really a boy in Italy

indicators.note: the name is held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A name that is a girl's in England is really a boy's in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a boy in Italy' completes the joke: Andrea is a girl's name in England and a boy's name in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea is a female first name in England, though male in Italy.

clue.text: No. 1's information on spa outbuilding

indicators.note: information is placed on, after, the spa

parts.note: a hydro is a spa hotel offering water treatments
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone seeks details about a building at a health spa.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen is the chemical element with atomic number 1; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Swift men, apparently got up thus, love horses' food

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: so means thus
O is love, zero in tennis
hay is fodder for horses

explanation.surface: Jonathan Swift's men, dressed up, like horses' fodder.
explanation.walkthrough: Yahoos are the brutish humans in Swift's Gulliver's Travels, ruled by horses, which fits 'horses' food'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yahoos are the degraded humanlike creatures in Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: No. 76, the big one — don't talk about it

parts.note: OS is outsize, a big clothing size

indicators.note: the silence word goes around the letter for one

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum
I is one

explanation.surface: A dramatic hush around element 76: the big one nobody mentions.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmium is the chemical element with atomic number 76.

clue.text: When to shoot, say, at the workplace?

indicators.note: signals the words are to be spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: orders to shoot on sight say when to fire

explanation.surface: A film director asks when to start shooting at the location.
explanation.definitionFit: On site means at the place of work, such as a building site.

clue.text: No. 15, Venus anadyomene

definitions.meaning: Venus rising, the planet appearing as the morning star

explanation.definitionFit: Phosphorus is element 15 and also the ancient name for Venus as the morning star.

clue.text: No. 30 and last, limited?

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
Inc, incorporated, is the American equivalent of a limited company

explanation.surface: Element 30 comes last, and perhaps is a limited company.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is the chemical element with atomic number 30.

clue.text: Almost the last word in fermentation

definitions.text: Almost the last word in fermentation

parts.words: Almost the last word in fermentation
parts.note: reads as an authority on brewing, but describes a word for a ferment that sits almost at the end of the dictionary

explanation.definitionFit: A zyme is a ferment, and the word comes near the very end of the alphabetical dictionary.

clue.text: No. 27, as Latvian to Lithuanian

parts.note: a Latvian stands to a Lithuanian as a fellow, co-, member of the same group
a Latvian is a Balt

explanation.surface: Element 27 compares neighbouring Baltic peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: Latvians and Lithuanians are both Balts, so to a Lithuanian a Latvian is a co-Balt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is the chemical element with atomic number 27.

clue.text: No. 51 is opposed to un-English currency

parts.note: anti means opposed

indicators.note: the E for English is removed

parts.note: money is currency

explanation.surface: Element 51 objects to foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is the chemical element with atomic number 51.
